Trace, implement and test: 17.08.Circus Tower

Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

Original source context
class BinaryIndexedTree {
public:
    BinaryIndexedTree(int _n)
        : n(_n)
        , c(_n + 1) {}

    void update(int x, int val) {
        while (x <= n) {
            c[x] = max(c[x], val);
            x += x & -x;
        }
    }

    int query(int x) {
        int s = 0;
        while (x > 0) {
            s = max(s, c[x]);
            x -= x & -x;
        }
        return s;
    }

private:
    int n;
    vector<int> c;
};

class Solution {
public:
    int bestSeqAtIndex(vector<int>& height, vector<int>& weight) {
        int n = height.size();
        vector<pair<int, int>> people;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
            people.emplace_back(height[i], weight[i]);
        }
        sort(people.begin(), people.end(), [](const pair<int, int>& a, const pair<int, int>& b) {
            if (a.first == b.first) {
                return a.second > b.second;
            }
            return a.first < b.first;
        });
        vector<int> alls = weight;
        sort(alls.begin(), alls.end());
        alls.erase(unique(alls.begin(), alls.end()), alls.end());
        BinaryIndexedTree tree(alls.size());
        int ans = 1;
        for (auto& [_, w] : people) {
            int x = lower_bound(alls.begin(), alls.end(), w) - alls.begin() + 1;
            int t = tree.query(x - 1) + 1;
            ans = max(ans, t);
            tree.update(x, t);
        }
        return ans;
    }
};
